title: Finding the minimum and maximum of an array

visuals.title: Running minimum and maximum over a list
All values negative: why max must start from a[0]

goal: After this you can find the smallest and largest value in an array and their positions, explain why we start from a[0], and understand the idea of the second largest.
warmup: Five cricketers finish an innings. The scorer wants the top scorer. He looks at the first player's score and says 'best so far'. Then he checks each next player: if the score is higher, that player becomes the new best. At the end, whoever is 'best so far' is the top scorer. He never needs to look at anyone twice. Finding the maximum in an array is exactly this, and the minimum is the same story with 'lower' instead of 'higher'.
definition: The maximum is the largest value and the minimum is the smallest value in an array. We find them with one loop and a variable that remembers the best value seen so far. We start that variable with the first element a[0] and then compare it with each remaining element. If a new element beats it, we replace it. We often also remember the position (index) of the best value.
howItWorks: Watch the minmax visual. First maxVal is set to a[0], because before looking at anything the first element is the only candidate. The loop then starts from i = 1 (there is no need to compare a[0] with itself). At every step: if a[i] > maxVal then maxVal = a[i] and maxPos = i. For the minimum, the test is a[i] < minVal. After the loop, maxVal holds the largest value and maxPos its index. Important: never start maxVal at 0. If every value is negative (for example -8, -3, -15) then 0 would beat them all and you would report 0, a number that is not even in the array. Starting with a[0] is always correct. Second largest idea: first find the position of the maximum, then run a second loop that finds the largest among the other positions.

worked.problem: Read n values (at most 20), which may be negative. Print the maximum, the minimum and the range (maximum minus minimum).
pseudocode: READ n and the n values
FOR i = 1 TO n - 1: IF a[i] > maxVal THEN maxVal = a[i]; IF a[i] < minVal THEN minVal = a[i]
PRINT maxVal, minVal and maxVal - minVal

examTips: Always initialise max and min with a[0], never with 0 (values may be negative).
The loop can start from i = 1, because a[0] is already the first candidate.
Max uses >, min uses <. Use two separate if statements to find both in one loop.
To report the position, update the index in the same block as the value.
With strict > the FIRST maximum is kept; with >= the LAST one is kept.
romanSummary: Maximum ya minimum nikalne ke liye pehle a[0] ko best maan lo, phir baaki elements se compare karo.
max ko kabhi 0 se shuru mat karo, kyun ke agar sab numbers negative hon to 0 galat jawab ban jata hai.
Jab a[i] > maxVal ho to maxVal = a[i] aur maxPos = i kar do. Minimum ke liye a[i] < minVal.
Second largest ke liye pehle max ki position nikalo, phir baaki elements mein se sab se bara dhoondo.

practice.prompt: Why do we start maxVal with a[0] and not with 0?
options: Because all the values may be negative
Because a[0] is always the largest
practice.answer: Because all the values may be negative
practice.hint: What if every element is below zero?
practice.explanation: If all values are negative, 0 would beat them all and be reported as the maximum even though it is not in the array.

practice.hint: m always holds the best value so far.
practice.explanation: m grows from 4 to 9 and stays 9 because the second 9 and 6 are not bigger.

practice.hint: 9 appears twice. Does a strict > move p for the second 9?
practice.explanation: p becomes 1 when 9 is met. At index 3 the test 9 > 9 is false, so p stays 1: the first maximum is kept.

practice.hint: With >=, an equal value also replaces the old one.
practice.explanation: p becomes 1, then at index 3 the test 9 >= 9 is true, so p becomes 3: the last maximum.

practice.hint: Is there any number in this array that is bigger than 0?
practice.explanation: The original prints 0 because no element is above 0. Starting from a[0] gives the correct answer, -2.

practice.hint: Start from the first element. The smaller one wins.
practice.explanation: minVal starts at a[0], the loop starts at index 1, and the test is a[i] < minVal.

practice.prompt: Write a program that reads 5 integers and prints the minimum value and its index.
practice.hint: Read first with one loop, then search with a second loop that starts at 1.
practice.explanation: Keep both the value and the index. Update both in the same block when a smaller element appears.

practice.prompt: In the max loop for (int i = 1; ...) why can i start at 1?
options: a[0] is already the first candidate
The first element is never needed
practice.answer: a[0] is already the first candidate
practice.hint: What does maxVal hold before the loop?
practice.explanation: maxVal = a[0] was set before the loop, so comparing a[0] with itself is a waste.

quiz.prompt: Which variable keeps the best value found so far?
quiz.explanation: maxVal is updated every time a bigger element is found.
A new element becomes the minimum when it is smaller than the current one.

quiz.prompt: int a[3] = {-5, -2, -9}; int mx = 0; (loop as usual). What does mx hold at the end?
quiz.explanation: Nothing beats 0, so mx stays 0: a wrong answer. Starting from a[0] would give -2.

quiz.prompt: To get the POSITION of the maximum, what must change in the same block as maxVal = a[i]?
quiz.explanation: The index i is the position of the new best value.

quiz.prompt: To find the second largest value, what is a safe approach?
options: Find the position of the max, then search the largest among the other positions
quiz.answer: Find the position of the max, then search the largest among the other positions
quiz.hint: Remove the first winner from the contest.
quiz.explanation: A second loop that skips the maximum's index finds the next best value.
